alerts.title: Carbamazepine–DTG interaction causing virologic failure
alerts.message: Guidelines list carbamazepine as a contraindication for DTG initiation, noting it decreases DTG levels by 30–70%. The patient started carbamazepine 2 weeks ago and now has a detectable viral load (1,240 copies/mL) despite good adherence and prior suppression (<50 copies/mL). The temporal relationship strongly implicates reduced DTG exposure from this interaction. The clinician's plan addresses carbamazepine toxicity but does not address the DTG interaction or the rising viral load.

evidence.recommended_action: Switch carbamazepine to valproic acid per guidelines, or replace DTG with an alternative ART regimen. Send genotype resistance testing given the detectable viral load.

alerts.title: Carbamazepine toxicity with hyponatraemia and elevated ALT
alerts.message: Carbamazepine level is 14 mcg/mL (therapeutic 4–12), with symptoms of ataxia, nystagmus, tremor, dizziness, and headaches. Hyponatraemia (Na 128 mmol/L) is also consistent with carbamazepine-related SIADH. ALT 68 U/L may reflect hepatic effects of carbamazepine, valproate, or both. The clinician plans to reduce the carbamazepine dose, but given the contraindication with DTG, switching to valproic acid would address both toxicity and the interaction.

evidence.recommended_action: Reduce carbamazepine dose as planned, but strongly consider switching to valproic acid to simultaneously resolve toxicity and the DTG interaction.

alerts.title: Genotype testing missing for new detectable viral load
alerts.message: Guidelines recommend genotype testing when viral load is detectable, as virological monitoring indicates treatment failure and the need to switch therapy to prevent accumulation of drug-resistance mutations. The patient's viral load rose from <50 to 1,240 copies/mL, but the clinician's plan does not include genotype testing. Given the likely DTG–carbamazepine interaction as the cause, resistance mutations may not yet be present, but genotype confirmation is still guideline-mandated.

evidence.recommended_action: Order genotype resistance testing and repeat viral load after resolving the carbamazepine–DTG interaction to confirm whether suppression is restored.
